title: Agentic App Architecture Spec
description: Describes an agentic LLM application's shape across five architecture axes: interaction transparency, state/history/memory, context & caching economics, capability integration, and execution substrate & side effects.

appName.description: Human-readable name of the app being architected.

transparency.description: Axis 1: interaction surface & transparency of thinking/tool use.

thinkingVisible.description: Agent reasoning/thinking is streamed or shown to the human, inline or collapsible.

toolUseVisible.description: Tool calls and their results are visible, not hidden behind a bare chat bubble.

planBeforeAct.description: A plan is shown before consequential actions execute.

interruptible.description: The human can interrupt/steer the agent mid-run, not just before it starts.

stateModel.description: Axis 2: state, history & memory beyond the raw conversation transcript.

durableHistory.description: Conversation history persists across process restarts and is resumable.

forking.description: A thread can be forked to explore alternates without destroying the main line.

rename.description: Sessions/threads can be renamed and organized.

episodicMemory.description: Salient facts are promoted to durable memory with TTLs/blob-promotion, recallable by relevance.

contextStrategy.description: Axis 3: context-window budgeting and caching economics.

caching.description: Prompt caching is used for stable prefixes (system prompt, tool schemas, pinned context).

eviction.description: Stale turns are evicted or summarized instead of growing the window unbounded.

memoryPromotion.description: Durable facts are promoted out of the context window into memory rather than re-paid-for every turn.

capabilities.description: Axis 4: how the agent gains powers (tools, skills, MCP) and how secrets reach them.

tools.description: The agent has tool-use capability (function calling / tool schemas).

skills.description: The agent has progressive-disclosure skill packs available.

coreSize.description: Number of MCP servers always loaded globally (the always-on core).

perProjectSpecialists.description: Project-specific MCP servers are configured per-project rather than folded into the global core.

mode.description: How secrets reach tool invocations. hidden-stdin/secret-store/env-scoped are safe; argv/inline/none are not.

execution.description: Axis 5: where the agent's actions land and how side effects are gated.

agentType.description: Whether the agent's substrate is a code repo or a non-coding artifact/side-effect surface.

isolation.description: Coding: per-writer worktree/branch isolation. Non-coding: sandboxed execution for side effects.

sideEffectHumanGate.description: Irreversible or outward-facing actions require an explicit human checkpoint before executing.

artifactReceipts.description: Side-effecting work produces a durable, artifact-backed receipt.
